rationale: All four lenses plus standards ran and parsed cleanly, no spec gap and no decision_needed items; 10 findings survived triage (2 critical — a dropped custom/Ollama-searched model selection in setup, and a missing AC22 fallback notice on OpenCode/Codex — plus 8 major) against 6 dismissed as unreachable/below-floor (an already-guarded undefined-model branch, CSV comma/whitespace edge cases, a degenerate zero-model display string, an any-cast matching an existing pattern, and a stale-env claim contradicted by its own guard snippet) and 0 deferred. Reachability was hand-verified against real source for every patch-bucket finding except the Claude [1m]-variant keep-case and the new models-switch-prompt.ts UI (folded into CR-005), which keep their lens-derived grading uncovered by the review's ~26/30 tool-call budget, forcing confidence to low despite the clean lens roster and standards coverage_gap: false.

standards_review.notes: 15 commit subjects use allowed commitlint types/scopes, imperative mood, under 100 chars. One mid-branch WIP fix(agents) commit is tolerated pre-squash.

promptForModelsSelection (setup.ts:465-599) is ~135 lines / 6 responsibilities — see CR-008. Other touched code has return types and .js imports; several pre-existing files already exceed the 500-line guideline.
Diff doesn't touch attribution headers or JWT claims; CRITICAL checklist N/A. CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS/CODEMIE_CODEX_AVAILABLE_MODELS carry only model ids; no secrets logged.

findings.title: Docs contradict on models switch's scope
findings.problem: docs/CONFIGURATION.md says `codemie models switch` changes the active model "without touching credentials, reasoningEffort, or any other profile field", but docs/COMMANDS.md (and switchActiveProfileModel's own implementation) say it also writes haikuModel/sonnetModel/opusModel "when applicable" for Claude-backed profiles.
findings.impact: Both docs are part of this same change and directly disagree about a real functional side effect; a user relying on CONFIGURATION.md's blanket claim is misled about a write the command performs.
findings.recommendation: Correct docs/CONFIGURATION.md's wording to carve out the Claude tier fields, matching docs/COMMANDS.md's more accurate phrasing.

findings.title: Claude /model picker can omit the live active model
findings.problem: The CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS filter (`options.filter(o => allowed.has(o.model.replace(/\[1m\]$/, '')))`) runs after the tier-resolution block (lines 404-454) has already reassigned env.CODEMIE_MODEL to a retirement-healed model, but the filter has no clause keeping that active model, unlike OpenCode/Pi's equivalents.
findings.impact: If the healed active model isn't itself in the profile's stored CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS while other stored ids remain live, the narrowed /model picker can omit the model the session is actually running.
findings.recommendation: Add `|| option.model.replace(/\[1m\]$/, '') === env.CODEMIE_MODEL` to the filter predicate.

findings.title: Codex filter can drop the live active model
findings.problem: filterAvailableModelsToProfile intersects availableModels with CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS and falls back to the unfiltered list only when the intersection is empty; it never explicitly keeps env.CODEMIE_MODEL the way OpenCode's filterToAllowed and Pi's filterEntriesToProfile both do. setupProxy assigns env.CODEMIE_MODEL = resolution.selectedModel (a possibly retirement-healed model) immediately before this filter runs.
findings.impact: When the active model has been healed to a model outside the stale CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS while other stored ids remain live, CODEMIE_CODEX_AVAILABLE_MODELS silently excludes it; an explicit --model <that-model> is then wrongly rejected by assertExplicitCodexModelAllowed even though it is the model Codex is already running.
findings.recommendation: Mirror OpenCode/Pi: keep the resolved/selected model in the filtered result even when it falls outside CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS.

findings.title: AC22 notice missing for OpenCode/Codex catalog fallback
findings.problem: When CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODELS matches none of the live catalog, filterToAllowed (OpenCode/codemie-code) and filterAvailableModelsToProfile (Codex, codex-models.ts:506-516) both fall back to the unfiltered list with zero logging of any kind, while the equivalent Claude and Pi fallbacks both emit logger.warn.
findings.impact: AC22 requires a notice that the agent's menu still shows the full catalog; two of the four agents give no notice at all, so the acceptance criterion is only partially met.
findings.recommendation: Add an equivalent logger.warn(...) call in both fallback branches, matching the Claude/Pi wording.

findings.title: New filtering/switching integration points are untested end-to-end
findings.problem: Only pure helper functions are unit-tested in isolation for this change's new filtering/switching logic — never the real call site: OpenCode's beforeRun wiring of filterToAllowed into provider.models, Codex's three setupProxy branches, Pi's fetchAndBuildPiModels call to filterEntriesToProfile, Claude's [1m]-suffix keep-case, and the new models-switch-prompt.ts UI (fully mocked out in its only consuming test).
findings.impact: A regression at any of these integration points (wrong env var, swapped arguments, mis-ordered filter call, or broken render/key-handling) would ship with no test failing.
findings.recommendation: Add one integration-level test per plugin lifecycle hook asserting on the real output artifact, a keep-case test for the Claude [1m] variant, and a deterministic render test for renderModelSwitchSelectionUI.

findings.title: Tier-refresh network call aborts the whole model switch, and is untested
findings.problem: runModelsSwitch's Claude-tier-refresh block (proxy.fetchModels -> autoSelectModelTiers) has no try/catch; any failure propagates out, so ConfigLoader.switchActiveProfileModel (which needs no network access) never runs. All 5 cases in models-switch.test.ts mock AgentRegistry.getAgent to undefined, so this branch never executes in any test.
findings.impact: A transient network blip while merely refreshing Claude tiers denies a user a model switch that should otherwise be a pure local config write, and the coupling itself is unverified by any test.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the tier-refresh block in its own try/catch, log a warning and continue with tierOverrides: undefined on failure; add a test exercising this branch with a Claude-capable provider.

findings.title: installModel loop has no per-model failure isolation
findings.problem: The loop over selectedModels calling setupSteps.installModel has no try/catch; the profile is only built and saved afterward (step 4, line 296), so a failure installing the 2nd+ model aborts the whole setup before any profile is saved.
findings.impact: A transient failure installing one of several selected models (e.g. a mid-loop Ollama pull) forces the user to redo the entire setup, including re-pulling models that already installed successfully.
findings.recommendation: Catch per-model install failures, collect them, and still save the profile with the models that succeeded, surfacing which ones failed.

findings.title: promptForModelsSelection is an oversized, multi-responsibility function
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires functions under 50 lines with one responsibility; this function is ~135 lines and bundles empty-catalog manual/search entry, live recommendation fetch, the multi-select checkbox loop, custom-model entry, Ollama search re-entry, and the active-model follow-up prompt.
findings.impact: A single oversized multi-responsibility function is harder to test and modify safely, and is part of why CR-007 and CR-010 (both inside this function) went unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Extract the empty-catalog manual/search flow and the active-model follow-up prompt into their own named helper functions.

findings.title: Custom/Ollama-searched model silently dropped from multi-select
findings.problem: After picking "Custom model (manual entry)" or "Search Ollama library", the entered/returned id is added to the checked Set, but the next render's choices array is built only from the fixed models parameter, which never gains an entry for that id. Inquirer's checkbox can't return an id that isn't one of its choices.
findings.impact: Breaks AC3 for every invocation — any user who enters a custom model name or searches the Ollama library during multi-model setup silently loses that selection, with no error shown.
findings.recommendation: Extend the models array itself with the new id before looping back, e.g. `models = [...models, enteredId];`, so the next render's choices includes a real entry for it.

findings.title: Active-model follow-up prompt can default to the wrong model
findings.problem: defaultActive = preselected?.find(id => alreadyChecked.includes(id)) ?? alreadyChecked[0] picks the first element of the stored models array still checked, not the profile's actual active model. resolveProfileModels returns profile.models verbatim with no guarantee the active model is first, and the call site passes only the id list, discarding which one is active.
findings.impact: Updating a multi-model profile whose active model isn't first in the stored array presents the wrong model as the highlighted default; accepting the default silently switches the active model to an unintended one.
findings.recommendation: Thread the profile's actual model value through to promptForModelsSelection as a separate parameter and use it as the default when still checked.
